units.current: Your progress in those years came from peers who were your equals, people you learned beside more than beneath. You set your own standard and met it, and the confidence lasted.
Self-reliance pays in these ten years. You teach yourself what you need and find equals to train beside, and you come out of the decade more capable on your own terms.

You measured yourself against your peers in those years and would not ask the ones further along for help. Your progress came slower than it needed to, and what carried you was knowing every skill you gained was your own.

Comparison with peers drives you hard in these years, and the standard you hold yourself to leaves little ease. One equal who works beside you instead of against you keeps you going, and you grow because of it.
Friendships among equals defined those years, with people who matched your pace and asked nothing extra. You found a few friends who met you level, and you have kept some of them since.
Your friends in these ten years are equals, people with their own lives and their own strength. Your circle stays small and solid, and you trust it more than any crowd.

During those years you held yourself apart from most groups, sure that few people matched your standard. Your circle grew smaller than it had been, and you found the one or two friends who stayed were enough to carry you.

Company that truly matches you is scarce in these years, and crowded groups wear you out quickly. One steady friend carries you through the decade, and you value that friend more than a full calendar.

notes.issue: On six pages the heavy Twin and heavy Rival decades sit side by side and both carry the reader with one friend ("What carries you is one friend who never competes with you"), and the Twin's carry is not the Twin's own force (source: 渊海子平 论比肩, the Twin is the self's own strength).
notes.fix: "Company that truly matches you is scarce in these years, and crowded groups wear you out quickly. Standing on your own carries you through the decade, and you value a quiet evening more than a full calendar." (37 words)

units.current: Those years filled your life with lively company, friends who competed with you and pushed you on. You were at your best among a crowd of rivals, and you won their respect openly.
Rivalry turns friendly in these years, and people who compete with you end up on your side. You keep a busy circle through the decade, one where you give and receive in fair measure.
Friendship and contest mixed in those years, and more than once a friend took credit or a prize you had earned. The company itself got you through, and you learned to tell an ally from a competitor.

Comparison runs through your friendships in these years, and you notice who earns more and who wins more. What carries you is one friend who never competes with you, and you lean on that friend above all others.
You ease into your body in these years, with better appetite and better sleep and more pleasure in ordinary days. You enjoy your health through this decade, and you feel at ease in your own skin.
Your appetite and sleep were good in those years, and ordinary pleasures kept you well. You ate with enjoyment and moved without strain, and you felt at ease in your own body.
Rich food, late nights and easy evenings piled up in those years, and your energy dropped as the habits grew. A plain daily routine brought you back, and you felt the change within weeks.

Good food and long evenings cost you energy in these years, and the easy option wins more days than you mean it to. You hold steady through a simple routine you enjoy, and you keep to it because it gives you pleasure.
You become more outspoken in these years, and the people who like it like it a great deal. You gather an audience of your own, and you lose patience with company that asks you to be quieter.

notes.issue: "like it like it" makes the reader parse the sentence twice, and the clause adds nothing the next sentence does not say.
notes.fix: "You become more outspoken in these years, and the people who enjoy a sharp voice seek you out. You gather an audience of your own, and you lose patience with company that asks you to be quieter." (37 words)

units.current: In company you were the lively one in those years, quick with a joke and a sharp opinion. People sought you out for your wit, and you enjoyed being heard.
Things you said aloud cost you friends in those years, and more than one group left you out afterwards. You kept the people who liked your honesty, and those few saw you through.
Bluntness strains your friendships in these years, and some people take offence at what you meant as wit. The friends who stay value your candour, and you find them worth more than a wide circle.
You turn your thinking outward in these years, and you say in public what you used to keep to yourself. You are quicker and bolder with ideas than at any time before.
Ideas came fast in those years, and you spoke them aloud with confidence. You were quicker than the people around you, and you enjoyed proving it in argument.
Restless thinking ran through those years, and you argued with most ideas that came from above. Your mind rarely settled, and what carried you was one project worth all that energy.

You argue with more of what you are told in these years, and every rule you meet feels like a challenge. One piece of work big enough to take all that argument carries you through, and you are calmest on the days you finish something.
You widen your circle in these years, through travel and new groups and the people they lead you to. You make more new friends in this decade than in the one before it.
Your circle spread wide in those years, through travel, work and friends of friends. You met people easily everywhere you went, and several of them opened doors for you.

notes.issue: The By decade tab keeps any decade that ends at 10 or later, so a decade that opens in infancy is read with a lived line written for an adult, and a toddler's years name work, travel and standards (source: 渊海子平 reads a child's years by the 小儿 rules, upbringing and 关煞, not by standing and work; 三命通会 论大运 dates a decade from its start age, which the line must fit).
notes.fix: Rule (resolver): `resolveDomainView.byDecade` reads a lived decade only when `l.startAge >= DEC_MIN`, as `resolveDomains` already does for its last past decade (`depthResolve.js` line 273, `l.endAge >= DEC_MIN` becomes `l.startAge >= DEC_MIN`). If the owner wants those decades shown, add a child tense per god, domain and pole instead (10 Social units, 60 across the eight domains).

units.current: Acquaintances crowded those years, and you knew people in many places without letting many of them close. One old friend who stayed kept you steady, and you confided in that friend more than in anyone new.
You meet more people in these years than you can keep up with, and old friends see less of you. A small group who knew you before this busy decade stays close, and you return to them again and again.
You grow fastest in these years through pressure, a hard role or a challenge you choose on purpose. You come out of the decade stronger in the places that used to hold you back.
Challenges shaped you in those years, and each hard test left you more capable than before. You learned to face pressure directly, and the courage you built has stayed with you.
Those years tested you more than they taught you, with one hard stretch after another. A stubborn refusal to stop kept you going, and you came out tougher and more tired than you expected.
Setbacks arrive in these years without warning, and you are pushed before you feel ready. What carries you is the discipline you already have, and you end the decade tougher in ways that show later.
You carry more pressure in these years, and for once it suits your body. You are fitter and sharper in a demanding decade than in an easy one, and you stay that way while you keep sleeping.
Your body answered strain well in those years, and hard training or hard work made you stronger. You had energy for demanding days, and you recovered fast between them.
Strain gathered in your body during those years, and it showed first in your sleep. You pushed through on nerve, and you got through because a few people made you stop.

Pressure costs you sleep and energy through these years, and short nights add up faster than you notice. What carries you is rest and slow meals given their place in the week, and you recover fast once the pressure lifts.
You hold standing among friends in these years, and people ask your opinion before they decide. You are the steady one in your circle, and you take the part seriously.
Respect came to you in those years through how you conducted yourself among others. People saw you as fair and dependable, and you were asked to lead more than once.

What was proper ruled your social life in those years, and you kept company with people you were expected to know. You were respected and a little lonely, and you found ease with one friend outside that circle.
Duty shapes your friendships in these years, and social life feels more like obligation than pleasure. Your good name holds, and you find relief with the friends who expect nothing formal from you.

You turned inward in those years, into subjects few people around you shared. You spent long stretches alone with your thinking, and you came out of it with work that still feels like the most important you have done.

notes.issue: The heavy decade names almost no cost and closes on a triumph, so it reads as the helping line ("Your thinking grew original, and you trusted hunches that later proved right").
notes.fix: "You turned inward in those years, into subjects few people around you shared, and work you owed others waited. You spent long stretches alone with your thinking, and what carried you was the one idea you saw through to the end."

notes.issue: A heavy decade must name its cost and what carried the reader. This one reads as the best decade of the reader's life and reads better than the helping line. It also repeats "few people around you shared", which the Alchemist's year line and month beat echo ("people around you" three times on D178). Classical ground: a decade bringing the unwanted god is a burden (子平真诠, 论行运).
notes.fix: "You turned inward in those years, into subjects nobody near you could follow. The long stretches alone left you out of step with the people close to you, and what carried you was one piece of work you still count among your best."

units.current: Your mind turns inward in these years, and long stretches of solitary thought leave work half done. One person who hears your ideas keeps you steady, and you finish more when someone is waiting.
Strange subjects drew you in those years, and you learned through instinct and odd sources more than set courses. Your thinking grew original, and you trusted hunches that later proved right.
Your intuition is sharp in these ten years, and unusual ideas find a use. You think in ways few others do, and people come to you for the angle they missed.
You grew in those years by going your own way, away from what was expected of you. The progress was real and nearly invisible, and you kept going on your own conviction while you felt behind.
Solitary searching slows you in these years, with many interests started and few carried through. One finished project gets you through, and you feel the decade's progress most on the day it is done.
Unconventional paths taught you most in those years, a strange course, a self-taught skill or a mentor outside the usual. You developed in your own direction, and the difference became your strength.
Private study pays in these years, and the things you taught yourself count for more. You grow in directions nobody planned for you, and the progress shows in work only you could do.

You let other people set your pace in those years, and you rested only when someone insisted. Their care carried you, and you learned afterwards to give yourself the same care without waiting to be asked.
Too much rest dulls you in these years, and comfortable days leave your energy low. What carries you is regular movement and a reason to get up early, and you feel better each time you have one.
Good care kept you well in those years, with regular meals, early nights and someone who noticed when you were tired. You recovered quickly from strain, and you felt safe in your body.
Support and good rest restore you in these ten years, and you recover quickly from strain. You sleep well and eat well, and your energy holds steady through the decade.
Steady study suited you in those years, and people who knew more than you gave your learning a firm base. You absorbed knowledge patiently, and much of what you know best dates from that decade.
Learning comes easily in these years, through books, good guides or a course taken at your own pace. Your thinking grows calmer and deeper, and you understand things you once rushed past.

Comfort in what you already knew held you in those years, and new ideas felt like a threat to it. You read and studied more than you acted, and the depth of what you had learned is what kept you going.
You study more than you act in these years, and your thinking turns cautious. Work that puts what you know to use carries you through, and you trust your own ideas again once you see them working.
Working alongside equals shows you your own shape this year, and you lean less on anyone's approval and more on your own judgement.
Friends meet you as peers this year, and you spend more time with people who do what you do than with those who look up to you.
Competition runs through your circle this year for the same invitations and attention, and you share your friends more widely than you planned.
Your circle widens this year through chance meetings and introductions, and you move easily between groups that never meet each other.
Private study and unusual interests change you this year in ways few people see, and you become more yourself out of public view.
Odd, specialist subjects pull at your thinking this year, and you study alone what few people around you would think to ask about.
You grow fastest this year where something forces you to, a deadline or a rival or a role with real stakes.
Pressure settles into your body this year as tension you carry without noticing, and you feel it first in your sleep.
Your thinking sharpens against the ideas you are handed this year, and you find flaws in what others accept faster than you can keep them to yourself.
Conversations with friends grow sharper and wittier this year, and you say the thing everyone else at the table was thinking.

notes.issue: The same image appears three times: in the Career year line ("you say out loud what colleagues only grumble about"), the Social year line and the seen line ("the one who says what the rest of the meeting was thinking"). The Almanac's year page prints the Career and Social lines together.
notes.fix: "Conversations with friends grow sharper and wittier this year, and you become the one your circle quotes the next day."

units.current: Meals, sleep and easy pleasures take a larger share of your days this year, and you feel how closely your body follows the pace you set.
Roles and expectations mark your friendships this year, a committee seat or a host's duty, and you are known for showing up when you said you would.
Your body leans on shelter and routine this year, warm meals and early nights, and you accept more looking after than you usually allow.
Books, courses and a patient teacher fill more of your evenings this year, and you learn most when someone else sets the syllabus.
